result:
The change is in place, all frontend. Nothing was run (no tests, typecheck, or formatter), as you asked, so the new tests are unverified.

## What changed

**`products/workflows/frontend/Broadcasts/broadcastWizardLogic.ts`**
- **Launch replaces schedules.** Before activating, launch now lists the broadcast's existing schedules and deletes them all, then creates the new one. This also covers relaunching as "send now", where an old schedule would otherwise fire later.
- **Move back to draft.** A new `moveToDraft` action sets the broadcast to draft, opens the wizard at the first step that needs attention (or review), and shows a toast. Failures show an error toast.
- **When it is allowed.** The broadcast must be active, have at least one schedule that is not completed, and have no send in progress. A paused schedule counts, so broadcasts already stuck by this bug can be recovered.
- **Stored broadcast now includes the new schedule.** Previously the stored copy came from the activation response, which predates the schedule.

**`BroadcastSummary.tsx`**
- Adds a "Move back to draft" button beside the title, shown only when the move is allowed. It shows a loading state while the request runs and is disabled while runs are still loading.

**Tests**
- `broadcastStatus.test.ts`: a table of cases for when a broadcast can move back to draft.
- `broadcastWizardLogic.test.ts` (new): relaunching a draft with a paused schedule deletes it and ends with one fresh active schedule; moving a live broadcast to draft makes it editable.

## Behavior to be aware of

- **Moving to draft keeps the schedule row.** This preserves the chosen send time in the wizard. The scheduler skips workflows that are not active, and the next launch replaces the row.
- **Old schedules are deleted before activation.** If activation then fails, the draft has no schedule row. The wizard still holds the send time in the open session, but a page reload would lose it.
- **Recurring broadcasts can be moved to draft between sends.** I read "live, scheduled" as "a send is still ahead". Say so if you want it limited to broadcasts that have never sent.

## Not done

- I did not make schedule `status` writable through the API. Replacing the schedule on launch fixes the bug without it.
- No docs change: I found no existing doc under `docs/` covering broadcast drafts or scheduling.
